subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam, and should the first implementation bridge to Gateway media/provider transcription rather than adding a separate native HTTP or command backend?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but implementation requires maintainer intent for native app versus Gateway ownership, microphone-audio routing, credential handling, private-network trust, fallback behavior, and overlay UX.

options.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default and add a final-text batch backend that reuses existing media/provider request controls and explicit fallback policy.

options.title: Fold into broader custom ASR design
options.body: Track this as the macOS PTT slice of the broader native ASR work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 until maintainers choose the shared native/provider contract.

options.title: Defer native backend selection
options.body: Keep native PTT on Apple Speech until the team has a broader voice-input plan across PTT, Talk, wake-word, and mobile surfaces.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default and add a final-text batch backend that reuses existing media/provider request controls and explicit fallback policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is in native macOS voice/PTT code, while the media/provider security details can be co-reviewed with provider owners.
